memory_leads.lead: Marine insurance is a layered risk-allocation system rather than one policy. Hull-and-machinery-type property risk, P&I-type third-party liabilities, cargo interests and other specialized covers can involve different assureds, underwriters, triggers and claims paths around the same voyage or casualty.

Insurance placement and renewal are recurring readiness states. Owner/operator risk information, vessel/fleet profile, trading pattern, loss history, deductibles/retentions and market appetite can influence whether cover is renewed, changed or made more expensive; exact terms and prices require Evidence.

P&I-type mutual liability cover has a structurally different role from ordinary vessel property insurance. It can sit around crew, collision, pollution, cargo, wreck or other third-party liabilities while the club/member relationship, mutuality and exact rule scope remain source-specific.

A casualty creates an insurance-notification and information-gathering chain before coverage or liability is resolved. Initial notice, preservation of records, survey or expert attendance, statements, repair/cargo information and authority findings may accumulate over time and can serve several insurers or claimants differently.

Local correspondents, surveyors, adjusters, experts and lawyers can act as operational interfaces between distant insurers/clubs and a vessel, port, claimant or authority. Their structural value is rapid local information and coordination, not independent proof of coverage or liability.

Claim estimate, accounting reserve, formal demand, accepted liability, settlement and cash payment are distinct states. Historical replay must not turn an early reserve or claimant demand into the later paid amount, and reserve revisions can preserve how expected loss changed as facts emerged.

Coverage position can remain uncertain while operational response proceeds. An insurer or club may investigate facts, reserve rights, seek further information or dispute parts of a claim while still coordinating practical response; exact legal effect and wording are Evidence questions.

Claims security or guarantee can be operationally important before final liability is decided. Providing acceptable security can help resolve an arrest, detention-like commercial hold or authority/claimant demand so the vessel or cargo can move, while exact security instruments and legal sufficiency vary by context.

Liability defence and settlement are trajectories rather than a single outcome. Fact development, jurisdiction, claimant negotiation, litigation/arbitration risk, contribution among parties and commercial cost can change expected settlement paths without this Memory pass assigning fault.

Recoveries create a second financial path after an insured payment or loss. Rights against responsible third parties, other insurers, contractual counterparties or shared-loss mechanisms may be pursued later, so gross loss, net retained loss and eventual recovery should not be collapsed.

Pooling and reinsurance spread large or correlated marine losses beyond the first insurer or mutual club. The structural state is layered loss transfer and accumulation management; exact pool thresholds, treaty terms, market participants and recoveries require dated Evidence.

Insurance is also an information and loss-prevention system. Claims experience, surveys, condition/risk concerns and recurring loss patterns can feed recommendations, deductibles, pricing, renewal appetite or operational changes, linking past losses to future safety and risk-selection behavior without making a compliance judgment.

Insurance availability and cost can affect more than claim reimbursement. Financing/covenants, charterer or cargo-counterparty confidence, port/security acceptance, route or cargo risk selection and willingness to operate in higher-risk areas can all depend on credible risk-transfer capacity.

P030 casualty/salvage response is refined because physical stabilization and financial-risk response run in parallel: survey attendance, claim notice, security, reserve development and recovery can continue long after immediate salvage or towage ends.

P031 investigation/known-time is refined because insurers, clubs, claimants and authorities may learn facts on different timelines; an official investigation state and an insurer's coverage/reserve state are related but not identical information histories.

P042 crew compensation is refined by separating the seafarer/beneficiary claim-support lifecycle from the owner's broader liability-risk-transfer chain. A household-support payment state and an insurer/club reimbursement or reserve state can differ in timing and scope.

Atlas counterparty risk is refined because solvency and credit confidence include not only owner/charterer/yard/bank health but also the credibility, limits and collectability of risk-transfer and claims-security counterparties.

The atlas already captures operational leverage, capital cycles and counterparty risk broadly; P044 adds the insurance/claims state machine rather than restating that large losses affect cash flow and financing.

Known-time, no-lookahead and claim-scoped authority are already Baseline semantics; P044 applies them to notices, reserves, coverage positions, settlements, recoveries and loss-prevention feedback without asserting a specific policy outcome.

reviewed_no_specific_memory.reason: Coverage and pricing turn on exact contract/rule wording and dated market facts; blind Memory retains only structural role and state distinctions.
Case facts, coverage, fault, damages, settlements and recoveries require claim-scoped Evidence; this pass makes no coverage or liability determination.
Provider identity, capability, membership, financial strength and historical role are organization-specific claims requiring Evidence.
Pool/reinsurance structures, security acceptance and current pricing/capacity are time-sensitive contractual/market claims requiring authoritative source-first material.

stop_reason: The insurance/claims chain is populated from placement/renewal and cover-role separation through casualty notice, local response/survey, reserve development, coverage uncertainty, security, defence/settlement, payment/recovery, pooling/reinsurance and loss-prevention feedback. Further recall becomes policy-wording-, premium/limit-, club-rule-, case-, provider-, treaty-, current-market- or jurisdiction-specific.
truth_boundary: Memory-only orientation; no policy coverage, liability, fault, claim value, reserve adequacy, settlement, security sufficiency, insurer/club membership, financial strength, pool/reinsurance term, premium or current insurance-market condition is verified.
